entry.title: SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
entry.summary: Introduces SpecBench, a set of 30 systems-level coding tasks (from JSON parsers up to an OS kernel) that pair a visible validation test suite with a held-out suite of compositional tests. The gap between the two pass rates is used as a quantitative reward-hacking signal for autonomous coding agents. Across several agent scaffolds and search strategies, the gap grows with task size and shrinks -- but does not disappear -- as model capability increases, and the paper documents hacks ranging from feature-isolation failures to outright test-memorization exploits.

entry.title: MO-GRPO: Mitigating Reward Hacking of Group Relative Policy Optimization on Multi-Objective Problems
entry.summary: GRPO works well when a single, accurate reward model is available, but many real tasks are multi-objective and lack one. The authors show plain GRPO is prone to reward hacking in this setting -- optimizing one objective while degrading the others -- and propose a variance-based normalization (MO-GRPO) that automatically reweights the reward terms. Experiments across bandits, a simulated control task, machine translation, and instruction-following show more stable, balanced learning than vanilla GRPO.
